findings.title: DPI Properties clipping
reproSteps: Open the packaged RSrender synthetic boring-log project
Resize to a constrained or high-DPI viewport
Open Layout and select a canvas or Contents item
Inspect the Properties pane and its dropdown controls
findings.observed: Inspector labels and dropdown values can clip or exceed their visible bounds instead of wrapping or scaling to the pane.
findings.resolution: The renderer derives an effective CSS viewport from native size and DPR, clamps pane widths to that viewport, and retains readable word wrapping. Fresh pass 04 showed the full Inspector before and after a successful Properties splitter drag at 125 percent DPI.

findings.title: Data em dashes
reproSteps: Open the packaged RSrender synthetic boring-log project
Inspect Project, Top elevation, Depth range, Total/completed, and Vertical scale
findings.observed: The Data ribbon displays em dashes for project values even though the structured boring-log page visibly contains project and depth data.
findings.resolution: Initial projection now populates the Data summary unconditionally. Fresh pass 04 displayed Project, Top elevation, datum, and depth controls; the controls use one horizontally pannable row rather than a clipped second row.

findings.title: High-DPI modifier chords were no-ops
reproSteps: Use the coordinate driver at 125 percent Windows scaling
Focus and edit a numeric Data control through window-message input
Send Ctrl+Z or Ctrl+Y through the original high-DPI fallback
Compare the visible value and page geometry
findings.observed: Plain high-DPI key and text input worked, but direct modifier WM_KEY messages did not populate Chromium modifier state, so Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y were no-ops.
findings.resolution: The driver now attaches the target input queue, supplies bounded modifier keyboard state and scan-code lParams, restores state in finally, and detaches. Fresh pass 06 visibly applied 10000, undid to 12025, and redid to 10000.
